test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following offenses has been newly and clearly defined under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mob lynching**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023**, which replaced the colonial-era **Indian Penal Code (IPC) of 1860**, has introduced **Mob lynching** as a specifically defined offense for the first time in Indian criminal law.
 
• Under **Section 103(2)** of the BNS, mob lynching is defined as an act of murder committed by a group of **five or more persons** acting in concert on grounds of **race, caste, community, sex, place of birth, language, personal belief**, or any other similar ground.
 
• The statute mandates severe punishments for those convicted of this offense, including **life imprisonment** or the **death penalty**, alongside a mandatory fine.
 
• While the **IPC** previously prosecuted such acts under general provisions like **Section 302 (Murder)** read with **Section 149 (Unlawful Assembly)**, it lacked a dedicated definition that recognized the specific socio-political nature of lynching.
 
• This legislative change follows various directives from the **Supreme Court of India**, notably in the **Tehseen S. Poonawalla v. Union of India (2018)** case, which urged the government to enact a special law against lynching.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evolution of Legal Definitions in BNS**:

 
 
• **Organized Crime**: Newly defined under **Section 111**, it covers activities like **kidnapping, robbery, and land grabbing** carried out by criminal syndicates.
 
• **Terrorist Act**: Defined under **Section 113**, bringing specific elements of the **Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA)** into the general penal code.
 
• **Defamation**: Retained under **Section 356**, but notably introduces **community service** as a non-custodial punishment option.
 
• **Sedition**: The term has been removed and replaced by **Section 152**, which penalizes acts endangering the **sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India**.
 
• **Snatching**: Now a specific offense under **Section 304**, distinct from ordinary theft.
